scope: Provisional chess judgements written before running the engine or classifier on this fixed sample. Empty output is not automatically correct. No statistical accuracy claim.
selection: Reached plies 2, 4, 6, 10, 11 and 12 in each of the three complete previously frozen ordinary games. No overlap with the original or adjacent root samples. No output-based replacement.

cases.judgement: Ordinary central development. No immediate tactical mechanism expected.
Quiet development against a restrained black centre. No forced material win expected.
Opening development. Central space and preparing castling matter more than tactical tags.
h3 gains a tempo on Ng4, which can retreat to f6. A single attack is not a fork or trapped piece.
The attacked knight can retreat. No reason to call the natural retreat a tactical combination.
Castling and development. Bg5 geometrically pins Nf6 toward Ke8 but ordinary pressure alone is not a winning pin.
Normal open-game starting position. No immediate forced gain.
Centre Game capture. Recovering the exchanged d-pawn with Qxd4 is not a free pawn win; c3 is an optional gambit.
Nxc3 recovers one of the two white pawns just surrendered in the gambit. It is development and partial recovery, not a newly won pawn.
Black has retreated and lost development tempi. White should exploit development; a concrete forced tactic is uncertain.
Qe2 supports e5 but also obstructs development. Black should develop or challenge the centre. Later king exposure cannot be attributed to this board yet.
f6 weakens the king. exf6 may be forcing, but alternatives to the game's Kf7 must be tested before claiming a mating attack.
Symmetrical knight development. No immediate tactic.
Standard kingside fianchetto setup. No immediate tactic.
Ordinary opening development. No immediate tactic.
Bf5 attacks Qd3, which should move. The f5 bishop is defended by g6, so Qxf5 is not winning a hanging bishop.
Qxf5 hangs the queen to gxf5. Hanging queen is the primary cause; the preceding bishop capture must be subtracted from the material claim.
White is down queen for bishop. Bxf6 Bxf6 is an equal minor-piece exchange, not a newly winning pin or exchange.
